Palestine Cinema Days Around the World: Six short movies

Various | 90’ | EN subtitles  



EN Join the 4th edition of Palestine Cinema Days Around the World in Filmhuis Cavia on 2 November, the 109th anniversary of the Balfour Declaration. 

A fragile ceasefire may quiet the headlines, but it does not stop the genocide. In Gaza, death continues through siege, starvation, displacement, and abandonment. As the world slowly looks away, we are reminded how easily Palestine can disappear from the news while its people continue to endure unimaginable loss. That is precisely why these stories must travel further and louder. At a time when silence is imposed on our existence, and our grief is treated as background noise, cinema becomes more than art; it becomes presence, memory, and resistance. MORE→

 

Entrance: Free on donation / Cineville

Palestine Cinema Days Around the World 

With Hasan in Gaza

Kamal Aljafari | 2025 | Germany, Palestine, France, Qatar | 106’ | EN subtitles  



EN Three MiniDV tapes of life in Gaza from 2001 were recently rediscovered.  A search for a former prison mate from 1989, leads to an unexpected road trip from the north to the south of Gaza with Hasan, a local guide whose fate remains unknown. 

This screening is part of ​​the 4th edition of Palestine Cinema Days Around the World.

CONTEMPORARY

On the Beach at Night Alone

Hong Sang-soo | 2017 | South Korea | 101’ | Korean, EN subtitles



NL De film, die uit twee delen bestaat, vertelt het verhaal van Young-hee, een actrice die Seoul heeft verlaten nadat haar affaire met een getrouwde regisseur openbaar werd. Young-hee ontmoet vrienden in de bioscoop, tijdens het eten en een drankje, en tijdens een wandeling op het strand, waarbij ze terugblikt op haar relatie. On the Beach at Night Alone is een typische Hong Sang-soo-film: minimalistisch, rustig en grappig, met een duidelijk autobiografisch element, aangezien zijn belangrijkste muze Kim Min-hee (uit The Handmaiden van Park Chan-wook) de hoofdrol speelt. Deze actrice werd zijn vrouw nadat hun veelbesproken schandaal de Koreaanse filmwereld op zijn kop zette en ervoor zorgde dat zij uit de mainstream werd verstoten. 

 

EN The film in two parts tells the story of Young-hee, an actress who left Seoul after her affair with a married director became public. Young-hee meets friends at the movies, for dinner and drinks, and a walk on the beach, reflecting on her relationship. On the Beach at Night Alone is a classic Hong Sang-soo - minimal, quiet, and funny, with a clear autobiographical element as it stars his primary muse Kim Min-hee (from Park Chan-wook’s The Handmaiden), the actress who became his wife after their highly publicized affair scandalized the Korean cinema world and left her ostracized from the mainstream.

CLASSIC

Les Feuilles Mortes #2

Memorias del subdesarrollo (Memories of Underdevelopment)

Tomás Gutiérrez Alea | 1968 |  Cuba | 96’ | EN subtitles  



NL Wanneer de Invasie in de Varkensbaai (1961) Cuba opschudt, vertrekken Sergio’s vrouw en vrienden naar de Verenigde Staten. Sergio blijft in Havana. Vanaf het balkon van zijn appartement ziet hij de stad veranderen en brengt hij zijn dagen door met vrouwen, boeken en lange wandelingen door de straten. Wanneer hij Elena ontmoet, begint een nieuwe affaire, terwijl de mensen en gewoonten van zijn vroegere leven langzaam verdwijnen. Om hem heen neemt de Revolutie steeds meer ruimte in. 

Alea verfilmde de roman van Edmundo Desnoes en verweeft Sergio’s herinneringen aan het Havana van die jaren. Een mijlpaal van de Cubaanse cinema en een van de meest kenmerkende films uit de revolutionaire jaren zestig.

 

EN When the Bay of Pigs invasion (1961) shakes Cuba, Sergio’s wife and friends leave for the United States. Sergio stays. From the balcony of his Havana apartment, he watches the city change and fills his days with women, books and long walks through the streets. Elena, a young woman he meets by chance, becomes the centre of a new affair, while the people and habits of his former life slowly disappear around him. Outside, the Revolution gathers pace. 

Adapted from Edmundo Desnoes’s novel, Alea’s film folds Sergio’s memories into the changing streets of Havana. Blurring the boundaries between personal experience and historical reality. The line between what Sergio remembers, what he sees, and what Cuba is becoming is never quite fixed. A landmark of Cuban cinema and one of the most distinctive films to emerge from the revolutionary 1960s.

CLASSIC

Europa trilogy

The Element of Crime

Lars von Trier | 1984 | Denmark | 104’ | English



EN The now rarely screened Europa trilogy was a major breakthrough for cult Danish director Lars von Trier. It moves between expressionism, surrealism, and avant-garde formalism; the trilogy constructs a dreamlike, often nightmarish vision of a continent haunted by its own history. Those films portray the European continent as an entity that lacks coherent cultural identity and is built on unresolved generational traumas as well as obsolete ideologies.

The Element of Crime, the first part of this triptych of moving images, could be described as an experimental neo-noir crime film. It follows the story of a detective who decides to take on his final case in order to attempt to catch a serial killer. He leans towards an unconventional method of hypnosis to help him solve the dilemma. Oneirical narration and long takes make this film a one-of-a-kind flick.

This screening is a part of our programme dedicated to Lars von Trier’s Europa trilogy. Please see the full programme below:

Windows, Beautifully Rendered – Machinima

Harun Farocki & Total Refusal | 2012-2022 | 74’ | EN subtitles  



EN What if movies shot in digital worlds tell us more about our world and how we conceive it than the reality surrounding us? What we see on screen in this program was never in front of a camera. These images were born digital: built, simulated and rendered by a computer. This evening is all about machinima, films made inside video games, and the works we’re showing use game worlds to look at the world, and at what it takes to make one look real. 

Harun Farocki’s Parallel I-III examines how game worlds are constructed, while Total Refusal’s How to Disappear and Hardly Working wander through game environments, looking at what usually goes unnoticed and turning it into a poetic critique of our society. MORE→

CLASSIC

Europa trilogy

Epidemic

Lars von Trier | 1987 | Denmark | 106’ | EN subtitles 



EN The now rarely screened Europa trilogy was a major breakthrough for cult Danish director Lars von Trier. It moves between expressionism, surrealism, and avant-garde formalism; the trilogy constructs a dreamlike, often nightmarish vision of a continent haunted by its own history. Those films portray the European continent as an entity that lacks coherent cultural identity and is built on unresolved generational traumas as well as obsolete ideologies.

Epidemic, the second instalment of the trilogy, is also the oddest and perhaps most elusive of the three. This self-reflexive creation takes the form of a quasi-documentary chronicle of the development of a screenplay for a film that was never made, blurring the boundaries between fiction and reality, creation and performance. Starring Lars von Trier himself as Dr. Messmer, the film unfolds as a truly bizarre journey into the process of filmmaking. Interwoven with this narrative is a parallel storyline depicting epidemics that have ravaged Europe throughout history, gradually transforming the fictional screenplay into a dark, apocalyptic vision.

This screening is a part of our programme dedicated to Lars von Trier’s Europa trilogy. Please see the full programme below:

07/11 | The Element of Crime (1984)
11/11 | Epidemic (1987)
18/11 | Europa (1991)

CLASSIC

Europa trilogy

Europa (Zentropa) 

Lars von Trier | 1991 | Denmark, France, Germany, Sweden | 113’ | EN subtitles 



EN The now rarely screened Europa trilogy was a major breakthrough for cult Danish director Lars von Trier. It moves between expressionism, surrealism, and avant-garde formalism; the trilogy constructs a dreamlike, often nightmarish vision of a continent haunted by its own history. Those films portray the European continent as an entity that lacks coherent cultural identity and is built on unresolved generational traumas as well as obsolete ideologies.

Europa, the final part of this triptych of moving images, is the most recognisable one in the oeuvre of the director. The film tells the story of the naive American of German descent who comes to the home of his descendants shortly after the end of the war. His desire is to help rebuild the destroyed city of Frankfurt. In the meantime, drawn into the love affair, his morals are put to the test.

This screening is a part of our programme dedicated to Lars von Trier’s Europa trilogy. Please see the full programme below:

Right Now, Wrong Then

Hong Sang-soo | 2015 | South Korea | 121’ | Korean, EN subtitles 



NL Hoe ontstaan relaties, en wat is er nodig om ze in stand te houden? De film vertelt twee versies van het verhaal van filmregisseur Ham Cheon-soo (geïnspireerd door Hong Sang-soo zelf) en zijn toevallige ontmoeting met Yoon Hee-jung, een kunstenares die hij in de stad Suwon ontmoet. In de klassieke stijl van Hong Sang-soo leren de personages elkaar kennen onder het genot van soju en eten, tijdens lange wandelingen in de kou en door middel van brutale eerlijkheid.

 

EN How do connections form, and what is necessary for them to persist? The film tells two versions of the story of film director, Ham Cheon-soo (inspired by Hong Sang-soo himself) and his chance encounter with Yoon Hee-jung, an artist he meets in the city of Suwon. In classic Hong Sang-soo form, the characters get to know each other over soju and food, long walks in the cold and brutal honesty.

DOCU

Lesvia + Mr. Dimitris and Mrs. Dimitroula


NL Lesvia brengt meer dan veertig jaar lesbische identiteit in beeld, en laat het conflict zien tussen de lokale bewoners van een klein dorp op het Griekse eiland Lesbos en de lesbische vrouwen die erheen kwamen op zoek naar liefde, vrijheid en gemeenschap. De film wordt voorafgegaan door de korte film Mr. Dimitris and Mrs. Dimitroula van dezelfde regisseur.


EN Lesvia chronicles 40+ years of lesbian identity and the conflict between the locals of a small village on the Greek island of Lesvos and lesbians who arrived searching for love, freedom and community. The film is preceded by the short Mr. Dimitris and Mrs. Dimitroula, by the same director.  

 

Mr. Dimitris and Mrs. Dimitroula 

Tzeli Hadjidimitriou | 2019 | Greece | 28’ | EN subtitles  



NL Dimitris leidt haar leven in Skala Skamnias, het conservatieve Griekse vissersdorp waar ze is geboren. Ze heeft haar stervende ouders verzorgd en woont nu alleen; eindelijk kan ze genieten van haar vrouwelijkheid door op straat te dansen op oude popmuziek, gadegeslagen door haar kat.

Hoewel ze door haar familie niet begrepen wordt, wordt ze geprezen door journalisten die verslag doen van de vluchtelingencrisis; haar veerkracht wordt prachtig in beeld gebracht. Ze blikt terug op de tijd die ze buiten Lesbos doorbracht en op haar dienstplicht in het Griekse leger. De film, waarin ze op liefdevolle wijze wordt geobserveerd en geïnterviewd door een lesbische filmmaker die zelf weet hoe het is om 'anders' op te groeien in een kleine, traditionele gemeenschap, getuigt van een gedeelde menselijkheid en wederzijds respect.

 

EN Dimitris lives her life in Skala Skamnias, the conservative Greek fishing village where she was born. She nursed her dying parents and now lives alone, able, at last to enjoy her femininity by dancing in the street to old pop records, watched by her cat.

Misunderstood by family but celebrated by journalists covering the refugee crisis, her resilience is captured by the camera. She recalls time spent away from Lesvos and conscription into the Greek army. Gently observed and interviewed by a Lesbian film maker similarly aware of what it means to grow up different in a tiny traditional community, their shared humanity and mutual respect shine through this touching biographical film.

+

Lesvia

Tzeli Hadjidimitriou | 2024 | Greece | 78’ | EN subtitles



NL Sinds de jaren zeventig voelen lesbische vrouwen van over de hele wereld zich aangetrokken tot het eiland Lesbos, de geboorteplaats van de Oud-Griekse dichteres Sappho. Wanneer ze in een lokaal dorp het paradijs vinden en een eigen lesbische gemeenschap opbouwen, laaien de spanningen met de lokale bevolking op. Beide groepen eigenen zich de lesbische identiteit toe, waardoor filmmaker Tzeli Hadjidimitriou – zelf afkomstig van het eiland en lesbisch – tussen twee vuren komt te staan. Ze brengt meer dan veertig jaar aan liefde, gemeenschapszin en conflicten in beeld, en onderzoekt wat het betekent om je geaccepteerd te voelen.


EN Since the 1970s, lesbians from around the world have been drawn to the island of Lesvos, birthplace of the ancient Greek poet Sappho. When they find paradise in a local village and carve out their own lesbian community, tensions simmer with the local residents. With both groups claiming ownership of lesbian identity, filmmaker Tzeli Hadjidimitriou—a native and lesbian herself—is caught in the middle and chronicles 40+ years of love, community, conflict, and what it means to feel accepted.

The Territory 

Alex Pritz | 2022 | Brazil, Denmark, USA | 85’ | EN subtitles  


Credit: Alex Pritz/Amazon Land Documentary
 

EN The Territory provides an immersive on-the-ground look at the tireless fight of the Uru-eu-wau-wau people against the encroaching deforestation brought by farmers and illegal settlers in the Brazilian Amazon. With awe-inspiring cinematography showcasing the titular landscape and richly textured sound design, the film takes audiences deep into the Uru-eu-wau-wau community and provides unprecedented access to the farmers and settlers illegally burning and clearing the protected Indigenous land.

Partially shot by the Uru-eu-wau-wau people, the film relies on footage captured over three years as the community risks their lives to set up their own news media team in the hopes of exposing the truth.

Chronovisor

Kevin Walker & Jack Auen | 2026 | USA | 99’ | EN subtitles (for non-English language parts)



NL "Chronovisor is zon­der twij­fel een van de meest opzien­ba­ren­de expe­ri­men­te­le lang­speel­de­bu­ten van het jaar en groei­de uit tot dé sen­sa­tie van het Internationaal Filmfestival Rotterdam. Dit op 16mm gefilm­de arm­chair mys­tery ademt de geest van Jorge Luis Borges en Umberto Eco. Een onder­zoe­ker, gespeeld door aca­de­mi­ca Anne-Laure Sellier, raakt geob­se­deerd door het ware ver­haal van de bene­dic­tijn Pellegrino Ernetti. Hij beweer­de in de jaren vijf­tig de krui­si­ging van Christus en toe­spra­ken van Cicero en Napoleon te heb­ben gezien met de chrono­vi­sor: een machi­ne die elk moment uit de wereld­ge­schie­de­nis via gol­ven kan oproe­pen op een tv-scherm.

Een bri­co­la­ge van pri­mai­re bron­nen, audio­cas­set­tes, voet­no­ten, ver­ta­lin­gen en VHS-ban­den vormt het visu­e­le zwaar­te­punt waar het fic­tie­ver­haal omheen cir­kelt. Een radi­ca­le film­vorm die doet den­ken aan expe­ri­men­te­le klas­sie­kers van Chris Marker (La Jetée), Michael Snow (So Is This), David Gatten en Nam June Paik." (ArtCinemaOFFoff)

 

EN "One of the year’s most stri­king expe­ri­men­tal fea­tu­re debuts, Chronovisor quick­ly beca­me the break­out sen­sa­ti­on of the 2026 International Film Festival Rotterdam. Shot on 16mm, this arm­chair mys­tery is steeped in the spi­rit of Jorge Luis Borges and Umberto Eco. A researcher, play­ed by aca­de­mic Anne-Laure Sellier, beco­mes obses­sed with the true sto­ry of Benedictine monk Pellegrino Ernetti. In the 1950s, he clai­med to have seen the cru­ci­fixi­on of Christ, as well as spee­ches by Cicero and Napoleon, using the chrono­vi­sor: a machi­ne said to be capa­ble of retrie­ving any moment from world his­to­ry via waves and dis­playing it on a tele­vi­si­on screen.

A bri­co­la­ge of books, cas­set­tes, foot­no­tes, trans­la­ti­ons and VHS tapes con­sti­tu­tes the visu­al cen­tre of gra­vi­ty around which the fic­ti­o­nal sto­ry orbits. A radi­cal cine­ma­tic form that recalls expe­ri­men­tal clas­sics by Chris Marker (La Jetée), Michael Snow (So Is This), David Gatten and Nam June Paik." (ArtCinemaOFFoff)

Brazil Unfiltered

Piripkura

Renata Terra, Mariana Oliva, Bruno Jorge | 2017 | Brazil | 81’ | EN subtitles  



NL Piripkura is het verhaal van een expeditie in het Amazonegebied van de laatste overgebleven leden van de nomadische Piripkura-etnische groep. Hun territorium kan alleen beschermd worden als er bewijs is dat ze er nog steeds wonen. Van de slechts drie overgebleven leden leven er naar verluidt nog twee in dit gebied. Om de twee jaar trekt een team van overheidsmedewerkers wekenlang de jungle in om hen te zoeken. Hun belangrijkste bezit is een fakkel die in 1998 werd aangestoken en sindsdien onafgebroken brandt. Het gebied waar ze wonen wordt omringd door boerderijen en zagerijen, waarvan de bijna onvermijdelijke uitbreiding met geweld plaatsvindt.

De film werpt licht op de tragedie die de inheemse bevolking van de Amazone treft: het systematische geweld dat tegen hen wordt gebruikt is een constante dreiging. Ondanks de indrukwekkende veerkracht en vasthoudendheid van de laatste Piripkura blijft een onvermijdelijke vraag in de lucht hangen: hoe lang kan dit nog duren? TRAILER

Winnaar van de Amsterdamse Mensenrechtenprijs op IDFA 2017.

 

EN Piripkura is the chronicle of an expedition in the Amazonian habitat of the nomadic Piripkura ethnic group’s last remaining members, who can only have their territory protected if there is proof they are still living there. Two of only three of them are known to still live in this area. Every two years, a team of governmental workers trek into the jungle for weeks in search of them. Their most important possession is a torch that was lit in 1998 and has remained so ever since. The area where they live is encircled by farms and sawmills, whose almost inevitable expansion is taking place through violent means.

The film sheds light on the tragedy befalling indigenous Amazon people: the systematic violence used against them is a constant menacing presence. Despite the impressive resilience and tenacity of the last of the Piripkura, an inevitable question hangs in the air: how long can it last? TRAILER

Winner of the Amsterdam Human Rights Award at IDFA 2017.

CLASSIC

The Color Wheel 

Alex Ross Perry | 2011 | USA | 83’ | EN subtitles  



EN What says Christmastime like fucked-up family relationships? Meet J.R. and Colin, the dysfunctional siblings at the heart of Alex Ross Perry’s often-overlooked mumblecore black comedy The Color Wheel (2011), his second feature in a filmography that includes eccentric indie gems like Listen Up Philip (2014) and Pavements (2024).

Aspiring news anchor J.R. needs to collect her belongings from her college-professor-turned-ex-lover’s apartment and drags aspiring writer Colin (played by Perry) along for the ride, ostensibly for moral support. What should be a quick errand spirals into an existential nightmare, with the two cynics constantly bickering to tear each other down, only to reveal a shared insecurity about their worth in a dazzling yet vaguely threatening world.

Shot on gritty black-and-white 16mm film by O.G. mumblecore cinematographer Sean Price Williams, it’s a dark ride that jostles between the cynicism and sincerity definitive of the post-2010s era. As Perry wrote, “I wanted to see if people could allow themselves to be embraced by something that’s unlikable and potentially upsetting.”

Dag van de Korte Film

Nederlands programma met Q&A

Various | 2025-2026 | NL | 94’ | EN subtitles 



NL Op de kortste dag van het jaar, 21 december, wordt de Dag van de Korte Film gevierd. Met een speciaal filmprogramma trakteren Eye Filmmuseum, Nederlands Film Festival en Go Short bioscoopbezoekers op de beste korte films van eigen bodem. Korte film is spannend, veelzijdig en heeft voor iedereen iets te bieden. Ook is het hét medium waarmee jong filmtalent zich als eerste aandient. Toch krijgt korte film vaak weinig tijd op het witte doek. Om meer aandacht te geven aan korte films vieren we al een paar jaar De Dag van de Korte Film, op de kortste dag van het jaar, zowel in Nederland als in diverse Europese landen. Kijkers mogen zich verheugen op films van zeer talentvolle makers, waaronder maar liefst drie Gouden Kalfwinnaars: This Is Your Captain Speaking (Gouden Kalf Beste Korte Film), How to Catch a Butterfly (Gouden Kalf Beste Korte Documentaire) en A Shot at Art (Gouden Kalf Beste Hoofdrol Korte Film).

 

EN Short Film Day is celebrated on the shortest day of the year, December 21. With a special film program, the Eye Filmmuseum, the Netherlands Film Festival, and Go Short treat moviegoers to the best short films from the Netherlands. Short films are exciting, versatile, and have something to offer everyone. They’re also the medium through which young film talent first makes its mark. Yet short films often get little screen time. To draw more attention to short films, we’ve been celebrating Short Film Day for a few years now—on the shortest day of the year—both in the Netherlands and in various European countries. Viewers can look forward to films by highly talented filmmakers, including no fewer than three Golden Calf winners: This Is Your Captain Speaking (Golden Calf for Best Short Film), How to Catch a Butterfly (Golden Calf for Best Short Documentary), and A Shot at Art (Golden Calf for Best Lead Role in a Short Film).
